proof_summary: Assuming the first claimed identity, the shifted pairs \((a_n+1,a_{n+1}+1)\) follow the Fibonacci matrix recurrence; modular matrix exponentiation modulo \(p=195318521017\) shows that both \(a_{249580077006}\) and \(a_{249580077007}\) are divisible by \(p\). Their gcd is therefore greater than 1, but for positive \(x,y\) the defining value \(g+(x+y)/g\), with \(g=\gcd(x,y)>1\), cannot equal \(1+x+y\), contradicting the claimed identity at the next index.
